title: DEMO RELEASED - Crowned is playable!
author: Guilty_Cockroach6222
selftext:
After months of solo development, I finally hit that publish button. Crowned is a turn-based card game inspired by Hearthstone and Gwent, now with a free demo on Steam!

How AI was involved: I used AI-generated art as placeholder assets for all 60 cards. It let me focus on mechanics and systems first without getting blocked on art. The community feedback was clear though - the AI art killed the vibe. So I'm now rebuilding the entire visual identity as a pixel art fantasy redesign with a new name, factions and theme.

Honest notes:

* Solo dev, learning project - Godot 4, Steam, game design all at once
* AI placeholder art - being replaced with hand-made pixel art
* Rough edges exist - that's why it's a demo!

Mechanics work well: two factions, Rush, Taunt, Aura, AutoShoot, Buffs, coin system, vs AI, Spells, etc...

Would love feedback on gameplay and thoughts on the AI art to pixel art transition.

[https://store.steampowered.com/app/4709990/Crowned/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/4709990/Crowned/)

comments.author: KidLink4
comments.body:
Playing it as I type, so as to give you live feedback. Here we go! 

Bear in mind, this is literally just me writing what I am thinking as I encounter stuff and is in no way meant to be rude or dismissive. You've accomplished something we all dream of and you should be proud.

Off the bat, The font is a little tough for me to read. I can manage but it adds to eye strain. 

Ok, we get to pick cards or mulligan. I see modifiers on the cards but I'm not sure what they mean. Maybe we go through it later? 

OOOH Recruitment is a very unique second turn bonus, It might even be too strong. I love the creativity though. 

Coins = Mana -> simple and familiar, good choice. 

UI note - you're using colored text nicely, but maybe a little unclear at times. Infantry, Cavalry, Defense? What is Defense? Maybe like Armored? Front Row and Back Row are yellow, so are Unit Types - can make different terminology categories unclear. 

Oh, Step 7 and now Front Row is red, and now Ranged is green. I think maybe color doesn't actually mean anything. Something to think about. 

Step 8, Front Row and Back Row are both red now. I'm no longer paying attention to color. 

Step 10 - Cards with Rush do not sleep? Do cards sleep or become exhausted? Are these the same thing? I think probably. 

Step 11 - hm... I wanted to read Step 10 again but there doesn't seem to be a back button in the tutorial. Also, repositioned units go to sleep? Or become exhausted? Man, I really wish I could read step 10 again. 

Step 13 - Ok, this is a lot all jammed into one turn - I'm gonna skip the rest of the tutorial boxes and see if I can figure out the rest on my own. (And many, MANY other people will have skipped sooner) 

I'm out of the first section of tutorial now and am taking my turn. 

I played the peasant card, and it went grey, I assume this means it's exhausted or sleeping. Tutorial popped back up but I skipped it - looked like it just said how to end my turn. I see I have this recruitment card? I played it but not sure what to do now? -- Oh, got it. Click a card in the hand and it goes down by 1 coin in cost. Maybe could use some direction when playing an effect. I'll attack with my king now. I tried to drag it on muscle memory but didn't work - click, then click again. attacks. turn ends. 

Enemy turn kills my peasant and hits me. 

My turn again. I wish I had played the recruitment card better, then I could have had both peasants out on turn 1. Not sure when I'll get the chance to attack again, but my turn ends here. 

Get hit. 

My turn again. I wish I had read the tutorial more closely, but wow it was a lot of text. This card has ENV 20 and RUSH. Not sure what ENV means but RUSH I think means I can attack? Let's see. 

Yes, I attacked. 

Fatigued? This is new. I just take damage? Is this some way to keep matches short? Not sure I'm a fan. 

Just kinda playing through now. 

Ok, finished the tutorial. It seems pretty solid, and I hope you continue to receive helpful feedback. Don't give up.

replies.author: Guilty_Cockroach6222
replies.body:
Wow, thank you so much for taking the time to actually play through and write all of this , this is exactly the kind of feedback that helps me improve!

You raised some really valid points:

I know that font is to fix also the colors !

**ENV**  that's actually Evasion! It's a system where heavier armored units or cavalry are harder to hit with ranged attacks. Simple percentage system  if a card has ENV 60, archers have a 60% chance to miss that target. King = hard to shoot because of the armor,  horses for example 20 ENV hardder to shot  than infantry etc.

**Sleeping/Exhausted**  yeah same thing, my bad for mixing terms! It means when you play a card that round it can't attack immediately. Cards with RUSH (like cavalry) skip this and can attack right away. Started with "sleep" everywhere then thought "exhausted" sounded more fitting for an army  lesson learned, picking one and sticking with it

**Fatigue**  mechanic to prevent endless games. When your deck runs out you start taking damage each round  1 damage first round, 2 damage second round and so on. Forces players to be decisive!

**King modifiers** \- each King has a unique passive ability that buffs certain card types. So your King might give +1 attack to all Infantry  you'll already see those modified stats during mulligan.

***Card color system explanation:***

**Green border on hand cards**  you have enough coins to play that card

**Green border on board**  that unit can attack this turn

**Red border**  valid attack targets for your selected card. For example if enemy has Defense units, only those will glow red because you must destroy Defense before attacking other units

**Gold/highlighted border**  currently selected card that you clicked to attack with

I'm not giving up on this - actually planning to redo all the art properly with my own assets. This whole project has been a learning experience from day one and feedback like yours is exactly why I put it out there.

Really appreciate you playing it and being constructive about it. Means a lot

comments.author: _TofuRious_
comments.body:
Bit too much AI for my taste. That style of AI art is very generic and soulless, although high technical quality. Overall production quality of the UI/animations doesn't match the quality of the art making the whole visual experience really lean on the generic imagery of the cards.

You look like you have some really interesting mechanical ideas but visually I can't get onboard to even install it. 

My 2cents for the future world be to peel back the AI imagery and land on a design style that is easier to execute and integrate with a matching quality UI experience. I know it's easier to just get AI to pop out super high detail illustrations and rely on the high detail in the ai gen imagery to hold up the visuals but honestly I think your game is worse because of it.

But as always, art is super subjective so if you like it then who am I to tell you otherwise.
